context: A uni student interviews a manager about supply chains
purpose: Teach: 引き下げ/免除/落札/需給/補完/著名/完結/出入り

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間いただきありがとうございます。御社の調達戦略について何点か伺ってもよろしいでしょうか。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. May I ask a few questions about your procurement strategy?
lines.style: polite student interviewer opening with formal university research register

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: ええ、どうぞ。最近は原材料の需給バランスが崩れていて、現場は対応に追われていますよ。
lines.en: Yes, please. Recently the supply-demand balance of raw materials has been disrupted, and the field is scrambling to cope.
lines.style: weary mid-career manager candid tone with industry jargon

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。価格引き下げの要請が取引先から来ることも多いと聞きますが、実際はいかがですか。
lines.en: I see. I hear that requests for price reductions often come from business partners — is that actually the case?
lines.style: curious follow-up with hedged academic phrasing

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: ありますね。ただ、関税の免除が認められた部品については、こちらも価格交渉に応じやすいんです。
lines.en: Yes, there are. However, for parts where tariff exemptions have been granted, we can more readily accommodate price negotiations.
lines.style: explanatory manager voice citing policy mechanics matter-of-factly

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 公共入札で落札された案件の場合、サプライヤー選定はどう進めるのでしょうか。
lines.en: In cases where you've won a public bid, how does supplier selection proceed?
lines.style: probing question shifting topic with technical procurement vocabulary

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 著名なメーカー一社に頼らず、二社以上で相互補完できる体制を組みます。倉庫の出入り口の動線まで設計し直すこともありますよ。
lines.en: We avoid relying on one famous maker and build a system where two or more suppliers can complement each other. We even redesign warehouse entry-and-exit flow lines.
lines.style: detailed operational answer with logistical depth

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 興味深いですね。最後に、今のプロジェクトはいつ頃完結する見込みでしょうか。
lines.en: That's fascinating. Lastly, when is the current project expected to wrap up?
lines.style: concluding interview question with appreciative academic tone

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 来年の春には一区切りつくはずです。論文、頑張ってくださいね。
lines.en: It should reach a milestone by next spring. Good luck with your thesis.
lines.style: warm closing remark encouraging the student informally
